Hospitalisations and deaths from severe disease

Source: R/severe.R
severe_outcomes.Rd

severe_outcomes converts a rate of severe disease into rates of hospitalised and community severe cases and deaths, following severe_incidence_mortality in the postie package (1.1.0), so that the numbers line up with malariasimulation outputs processed with postie.

severe_outcomes(
  severe,
  ft,
  treatment_scaler = 0.42,
  ft_sev = 0.8,
  hosp_sev_cfr = 0.065,
  community_sev_cfr = 0.6,
  baseline_treatment = 0.1,
  severe_scaler = 1/0.8
)

Arguments

severe

Numeric rate of severe disease from the model, e.g. the severe column of severe_rates. The outputs are in the same units.

ft

Proportion of clinical cases treated in the simulation.

treatment_scaler

Reduction in severe disease from treating a clinical case. Default = 0.42

ft_sev

Proportion of severe cases that are hospitalised. Default = 0.8

hosp_sev_cfr

Case fatality ratio of hospitalised severe cases. Default = 0.065

community_sev_cfr

Case fatality ratio of severe cases in the community. Default = 0.6

baseline_treatment

Treatment coverage in the data the severe model was fitted to. Default = 0.1 (fixed in postie)

severe_scaler

Multiplier applied to the model severe rate. Default = 1/0.8 (fixed in postie)

Value

A data frame with columns severe_model (the input), severe, severe_hospital, severe_community, mortality_hospital, mortality_community and mortality.

Details

The model severe rate is first scaled by severe_scaler and then by the effect of treatment, (ft * (1 - treatment_scaler) + (1 - ft)) / (baseline_treatment * (1 - treatment_scaler) + (1 - baseline_treatment)). A fraction ft_sev of severe cases are hospitalised, with case fatality hosp_sev_cfr; the rest die with community_sev_cfr.

The case fatality ratios (6.5% in hospital from Reyburn et al., 60% in the community from Lubell et al.) and the hospitalised share of 0.8 are from Griffin et al. 2016 Lancet Infect Dis 16:465-72, supplement section 3.4.4. The treatment_scaler of 0.42 is a postie assumption based on Mousa et al. 2020 PLoS Med, and the 10% baseline_treatment is hard-coded in postie (the historical coverage in the Griffin et al. 2016 supplement).

Examples

# severe rate of 0.01 per person per year with 40% of cases treated
severe_outcomes(0.01, ft = 0.4)
#>   severe_model     severe severe_hospital severe_community mortality_hospital
#> 1         0.01 0.01085595      0.00868476       0.00217119       0.0005645094
#>   mortality_community   mortality
#> 1         0.001302714 0.001867223
